activities.title: Oral Language Development: Community Circle Time
activities.content:
Greeting
• Welcome pupils and have them sit in a circle. 
• Follow the normal greeting routine.
• Have the pupil that was just greeted, turn to the pupil on their right and greet 
them. This continues all the way around the circle.
Theme Discussion
• Before school starts, bring in two items related to the theme to show the pupils. 
Put the items in the center of the circle. If no items are available, draw two 
pictures on the board instead.
• Say: kanёm ki unjuundi bёjuk inja aci "Ngёnjӓr." Ngёko ngan ci ngi di pёncuaf 
uroond, a yandaar ni unjuundi bёjuk inja
• Hold up one of the items from the center of the circle. 
• Say: : We ci wёn wi?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer.
• Say: We wi nda purir wёn pёleentsin tsi undo ko wi?
• Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer. Repeat with the second item.
• Say: We wi ngёko ngi pac wёn tsi inja?
• Give pupils one minute to think. You may suggest they close their eyes to picture 
their response. Then choose one of the following options for discussion: call on 
3 pupils at random, Turn and Talk (have pupils turn to a pupil next to them), go 
around the circle and allow every pupil to answer (only if the answer is short), or 
have pupils take turns acting out answers.
• Encourage pupils to bring in their own items relating to the theme throughout the 
week.

activities.title: Letter of the Week
activities.content:
Learning Letter: "_a  _A"
• Write the small letter "a" very big on the board. Point to the letter.
• Say: Uwab wi, wi nja kёrowёn kanёm ki. Uwab umёnts wi aka bёruur /a/. Nda jun 
ngёja/a/.
• Point to the letter on the board or letter card, say the sound, have pupils repeat 3 
times slowly.
• Write the capital letter "A" very big on the board. Point to the capital letter.
• Say: Bёruur/A/. Nja ka win wël di ujuundi irim, katim iñaan, ni katim ucaak.
• Point to the letter on the board or letter card, say the sound, have pupils repeat 3 
times slowly.
• Point to the small letter "a" on the board or letter card again.
• Say: Iink ri uu naam dun di irim ilon.

activities.title: Writing
activities.content:
Learning Names
• Say: Nja ka juk pёpican itim inja bëlieng.Nja karuka kajuund, nja ka wёlёlӓr bёrun 
iñan. 
• Warm up exercise: have pupils push their palms together as hard as they can for 
10 seconds. Then release and shake hands for 10 seconds. Repeat two more times.
• Give each pupil their individual name card.
• Have pupils go through the following steps: 
1. Pupils trace the letters on the name card with their fingers.
2. Pupils trace the letters of their name on their desks or on the ground. 
3. Pupils write their name on paper. 
• Monitor pupils through each step to make sure they are forming the letters 
correctly. Provide guidance as needed either verbally or by writing the letter(s) for 
the pupil to trace.

lessons.homework:
•  Ask learners to teach their family members the letter name and sound they learnt  
 today.

activities.title: Vocabulary

Teach and Discuss New Words
• Words: 
Mlik                    Usieu
• Say: Nja ka juk irim iwalu itsёnk inja ja ka pe pёme katёtan uwar. Aka irim iwar tsi 
katёtan ki, yi ngёka yi pёjuk.
• Say the first vocabulary word, but do NOT write it on the board. Then have pupils 
say the word aloud. Repeat two more times.
• Ask pupils what they know about the word. Share the meaning of the word, using 
gestures or illustrations to support understanding. 
• If needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language.
• Repeat all steps with remaining word.

activities.title: Before Reading & Reason to Read
activities.content:
Comprehension: Visualization 
• Say: Ngёjaakëntsӓn ko wi katёtan ki pac wi. 
• Read the title of the story but do NOT show the illustration.
• Say: Tsi uwejatsu giingan pёfootu pu piban ko wi katёtan ki pac wi. We wi m win 
wёn?
• Give the pupils a minute to make the picture in their mind. 
• Turn and Talk: Have pupils turn to the pupil next to them to talk about what they 
are visualizing in their minds. After two minutes, gather pupils back as a group. 
Choose a good example you heard from a pupil, and share it with the class.
• Say: Inkri, nja ka kuklӓn ifootu ni katёtan nja ka teen bi inaam bi.
• Show the picture for the story.
• Say: We wi m win wёn tsi pёfootu pi u naam wi ni ko wi m win wi di uwejatsu?

• Give the pupils a minute to think about what was the same. Then call on a pupil at 
random asking for what they see. Make sure the pupil's description relates to the 
picture and the story.
Learn New Print Concepts
• Say: Aja ngёteen kafёlal, nja ka teen-na irim, pёloole, pёloole. Katёtan ka ka irim 
icumal yi nja kёteena yi pёloole, pёloole tsi kafёlal kan ci ki. 
• Hold up the book. Read the title slowly and point to each word.
• Call on a pupil at random to come and point to each word of the title as you read.

activities.title: Comprehension: During Reading
activities.content:
Read Aloud
• Read aloud the story. Point to each word as you read.
ULAAR NI USIEU MLIK 
Aka Ulaar ulipal, wi ka njakaa wi Ananse. Unu ulon, bënu buer pëyëk. Ulaar buer 
pëlofënts, a mtum kay, a u ŋal përaan mak. A ulaar ja kalip a usubal sub. A ngënu 
këpar anoor usubal subats. Bënu këyëk, a ufuts këfuts, a karëmbatsi ci ka kay rin. 
Ulaar ja u ko ka pën katsas mlik. A u jäp ipiets, aya bi ngëntunda, a u diang ito ikay, a 
u ya bi ngëtsia anoor uko winats mlik. Upën bi utsia mko, a ulaar win dul ko undëmb 
wi. Aci usieu tsi unats tsi ni mlik di bametsu pëtsiim ukaaru. Din a u tuk aband ri 
usieu a u nats a u ja, Um di ndu yil dun përaan mlik mi tsi usieu''?
Ulaar jej pëtiiu pëjuurna mlik, maa mtum wël buer pëtiin këts. Uko puririts pëka mlik. 
A u ŋal pëjej ilaak pëcik-na pëtsiim ukaaru, maa iñan wël tiinkënts; uko yilanats yul.
Anoor, ulaar yokësaräts. A uu wits kak din u win mbuk mko. Ulaar ja, ''lipan, man wat 
mbuk mi di bamtsu mlik, pëloole, pëloole, Aa uu roon din, bëwaar, bëwaar mlik jot 
përiangee.
Tsi utuami ko, mlik baandi iruj usieu. Ulaar ran aa utewan. Uliladӓr been wël, bi ujiitu 
wël ka bi u ka mlik.
Din ulaar pën pëtsëp ni ulilan, ni pësuets, ni pëparir pëpën bëtsas.

activities.title: Comprehension: After Reading
activities.content:
Factual Question: Review All
• Read the title of the story. Call on a pupil at random to answer each of the 
following factual questions:
Question 1: We wi ulaar do wёn katsas? (Ujaankёma: Mlik.)
Question 2: Tsum tsi ulaar win-na tsun mlik?(Ujaakёma: Di usieu)
• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct 
answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. Help 
pupils find the part of the story that contains the answer.
Inferential Questions: Main Idea
• Say: Katёtan kan ci ki, aka ko wi kuu jukan wi. Ko wi ci wën, ko wi katёtan pac wi.        
• Tsi katsas mlik Ananse, ka wën a nja ne, katёtan aci undo bi Ananse ro bi aa na ka  
mlik.

• Ask the pupils if they agree.
• Say: Përim pënjӓmp tsi katëtan ki "Ulaar ni usieu" aci bi Ananse ka bi mlik,  par ko 
umpe wi përëmb tsi katëtan ki aci  bi u pёn bi katsas mlik.  
• Repeat the sentence but prompt pupils to finish the sentence by saying what the 
story is mostly about.

activities.title: Learning Sounds
activities.content:
Sound Matching Game
• Write the letters that have been learned on the board. 
• The letters should be large enough for all pupils to see. Make sure they are evenly 
spaced out in a line that is eye level for the pupils. After writing each letter:
• Say: Uwab woom ci wёn wi? We ci wën bëruur wël?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Put the pupils into pairs and give each pair a letter card (use only the letters that 
have been learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.
• Say: Uci nja ko, a nda tsij kafёlal kan tsij ki uwab umёnts, wi ni bёfetsaru, ndu tsiji 
kul, ndii kuklän  kul ni uwab un ci wi tsi tsëko tsёpicanaani najukan.
• When pupils go to the board with their letter card, affirm the correct answer or 
attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Go through the letters that have been learned. Assist pupils as needed if they are 
having difficulty connecting the sound said with their letter card.
• As time permits, switch up the letter cards between the pairs of pupils.

• Gather all the pupil name cards.

• Hold up a name card. If the pupil is unable to recognize the name, say it aloud.
• Once the child comes up front, have them give two actions for the class. For 
example, "[Name] says touch your toes. [Name] says jump twice."
• Continue with several pupils as time permits.

activities.title: Learning Sounds
activities.content:
Sound Matching Game
• Write the following letters on the board: a, b, c, d, e and f. 
• The letters should be large enough for all pupils to see. Make sure they are evenly 
spaced out in a line that is eye level for the pupils. After writing each letter:
• Say: Uwab woom ci wёn wi? Bëruur boom bi u ka bun?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Put the pupils into pairs and give each pair a letter card (use only the letters that 

have been learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.
• Say: Mán ja pёrim a uci m tsij kafëlal kan tsij ki uwab umёnts, wi ni bёfetsaru nda 
jӓndӓri bёpicanaani najukan tsi, ndu kaban kul tsul.
• When pupils go to the board with their letter card, affirm the correct answer or 
attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Go through the letters that have been learned. Assist pupils as needed if they are 
having difficulty connecting the sound said with their letter card.
• As time permits, switch up the letter cards between the pairs of pupils.
• NOTE: Keep track of which pupils are having difficulty recognizing specific letters. 
Also see if there is a specific letter most of the class is struggling with. If this 
happens, stop and review the letter before continuing with the game.

Reviewing Names
• Say: Nja ka lesës ko wi ngёjuk wi tsi pёpican itim inja. Nja ka ruka ka juund, nja ka 
colan iñan inja.
• Warm up exercise: have pupils tap their fingers one at a time on their thumb (start 
with pointer, then middle, then ring, then pinky). Do one hand at a time. As pupils 
learn the movement, try doing both hands at the same time.
• Give each pupil their individual name card. 
• NOTE: Have pupils write their name on their paper. If pupils cannot complete their 
name, try to find a way to help them. For example, write the letters and have them 
trace. Another option: see if pupils are able to write their name without looking at 
their name card.

activities.title: Alphabet
activities.content:
Name Card 
Put all of the pupils' name cards on the floor or table. 
• Say: Uci ndu katimu par pёbi tsi bёrun tsi, tsasan katimu.Uci m win katimu,wёliin 
kafëlal tsi.
• Have pupils come up 2-3 at a time. When they bring you their card, point to their 
name and as they say it move your finger along the letters. Then have the pupil 
clap the syllables in their name.
• NOTE: Monitor which pupils are able to identify their name and clap the syllables, 
and those pupils who have difficulty. If pupils don't recognize their name, try to 
find a way to help them remember it. For example, write it in large print on their 
notebook or a piece of spare paper. Ask them to take it home and trace the letters 
with their finger a few times. If pupils have difficulty clapping the syllables in their 
name, clap with them as you slowly say their name.
